name: Cairde Designs
description: Websites for home-service businesses and some nonprofits. Cameron Denny, Austin, since 2018. A five-page site is $150 a month for 24 months, then $50 a month to maintain it, instead of a few thousand up front. His first site sold for $500.

mentions.evidence: Self-reported, Starter Story, 30 October 2026. Not independently checked. $6,000 of revenue a month. An average of $72,000 a year. 1 founder, 2 employees.
mentions.indieAngle: A website for one trade, billed every month instead of once.

whyItPrints: A plumber's website, sold as a subscription. The 24-month contract turns a one-off project into a monthly bill.
whyThisMatters:
Cairde Designs builds a short website for a plumber, a similar home trade, or a nonprofit, and bills it like a subscription. Cameron Denny, in Austin, since 2018. Five pages, a monthly fee for two years, then a smaller fee to keep it. The first site he sold was a few hundred dollars, once.

He says about six thousand a month, which the interview also writes as a yearly average in the same range. One founder and two employees. October 2026. I did not check a processor. The contract is what makes a website job recur. Without the twenty-four months, it is a project.

You pay every month so the site exists, instead of writing one large check.

Nonprofits are in the customer list along with home-service trades. The maintenance fee after month twenty-four is the smaller number. Two employees besides the founder. Austin since 2018. The first sale was a one-off, and the later offer is the monthly contract.

The twenty-four month term is the product. After that, the smaller maintenance fee is what they offer. I am not adding a stack or a city beyond Austin.
